title: Rohlmann 2011: VBR resultant force in sitting variants, relative to reference sitting postures
subcategory: sitting (seat type, trunk inclination, backrest, arms)
condition: sitting on stool/chair/office chair/bench/ball/knee-stool; trunk inclination; backrest declination; arm position

quantity.name: VBR maximum resultant force, relative
quantity.definition: RELATIVE: change of the maximum resultant VBR force (%) vs the stated reference activity measured on the same day (mean of patient medians)

source.authors: Rohlmann A, Zander T, Graichen F, Dreischarf M, Bergmann G
source.sample: 5 patients (4 M, 1 F) with telemeterised VBR after lumbar compression fracture (4 x L1, 1 x L3); trunk-inclination and seat-height tests in 4 patients

patients.implant_note: VBR replaces parts of the fractured vertebral body and the adjacent discs; posterior internal fixator remains in situ
patients.source: Rohlmann 2011 patient table p.871 (note: lists WP4 fixation T12-L2, whereas Rohlmann 2014 PLoS states 4-segment fixation T11-L3 for WP4)

protocol.summary: Maximum resultant VBR force; compared only within the same measuring day; median per patient, then average of medians.
how_to_simulate: Model each patient (protocol.subject_model) sitting on a stool (46 cm) with arms hanging
Vary one factor at a time as in data[].x (upper-body inclination -10..+15 deg; backrest declination 90-180 deg; seat type; hands on thighs)
Output: segment compression (or resultant force) at the VBR level; express relative to the stated reference
A whole-spine MSK model outputs total segment compression at the implant level, not the implant share; compare trends/relative changes unless the model includes the VBR and posterior fixator

subject_model.implant_note: VBR replaces parts of the fractured vertebral body and the adjacent discs; posterior internal fixator remains in situ

protocol.notes: Load measured on a telemeterised vertebral body replacement (modified Synex, 6 load components, accuracy ~2% force / 5% moment of 3000 N / 20 Nm calibration range) that shares the load with the posterior internal fixator, residual vertebral bone and bone graft; the VBR force is NOT the total spinal load.

data.x: upper body 15 deg flexion vs upright sitting on stool
upper body 10 deg extension vs upright sitting on stool
sitting on a chair vs stool
sitting on an office chair vs stool
sitting on a bench vs stool
sitting on a knee stool vs stool
sitting on a physiotherapy ball vs stool
stool with padded wedge (9.5 deg) vs stool
chair without back contact vs stool
office chair without back contact vs stool
leaning against the backrest of a chair
backrest at 180 deg (supine) - force as % of sitting relaxed
seat height 40 vs 60 cm: average force difference
data.note: median force tends to increase with seat height

extraction.from: Rohlmann 2011 abstract and Results text p.872-873 (Figs 2-6 not digitised)
extraction.uncertainty: text averages; per-patient values only in figures
extraction.check_notes: Re-read abstract and Results; all percentages match. Sign convention here: negative = reduction.

pass_rule.rule: relative change: model sign correct and |model - measured| <= half the inter-patient range (or 25 percentage points where no range is given)
